title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 75
paragraphs: The Scythians then take the seed of this hemp and creep under the felt coverings, and throw the seed upon the red-hot stones. It smoulders like incense and produces a vapour so thick that no vapour-bath in Hellas could surpass it; and the Scythians, delighted with the vapour-bath, howl like wolves. This is their substitute for washing, for they do not in fact wash their bodies at all with water. Their women, however, pound with a rough stone the wood of the cypress, cedar, and frankincense tree, pouring water in with it, and with the resulting thick paste they plaster their whole body and face. Not only does a sweet smell attach to them from this, but when they take off the plaster the next day, their skin is clean and shining.
